%A Harisnah, Shintia %A Idris, Fadhliyah %A Hidayati, Jelita Rahma %D 2026 %T Microplastic characteristics of seagrass leaves ( Enhalus acoroides ) in Malang Rapat and Berakit Waters, Bintan Regency %B 2026 %9 Seagrass; Microplastic; Bintan Island; Waste %! Microplastic characteristics of seagrass leaves ( Enhalus acoroides ) in Malang Rapat and Berakit Waters, Bintan Regency %K Seagrass; Microplastic; Bintan Island; Waste %X The seagrass ecosystem is a shallow marine plant ecosystem with high biological productivity but is now threatened by human activities, especially the disposal of plastic waste into the sea, which degrades into microplastics measuring 0.3 –> 5 mm. This study aimed to identify the characteristics and measure the abundance of microplastics in the leaves of Enhalus acoroides in the waters of Malang Rapat and Berakit, Bintan Regency. The research was conducted in March–April using the purposive sampling method, with samples collected during the lowest tide using a 50×50 cm quadrat transect. Microplastic identification was carried out by scraping the surface of seagrass leaves, followed by processing with H₂O₂, Fe₂SO₄, and NaCl solutions, and observing the samples under a microscope to determine the type, color, and quantity of microplastics. The results showed three types of microplastics, namely fiber, fragment, and film, with the highest abundance found at the Berakit location at the 100-meter point of 9.07 particles/cm², dominated by the fragment type (5.67 particles/cm²). The identified colors were brown, transparent, black, red, blue, and green, with transparent being the most dominant (19.81 particles/cm²). %U https://journals.sangia.org/ISLE/article/view/774 %0 Journal Article %R 10.29239/j.akuatikisle.10.1.69-75 %& 69 %P 7 %J Akuatikisle: Jurnal Akuakultur, Pesisir dan Pulau-Pulau Kecil %V 10 %N 1 %@ 2598-8298 %8 2026-01-12 %7 2026-05-31
